searchText: FYI: I'm analyzing network traffic transmit/received interactions between clients. Taking 5% Pyrmont nodes offline at a time to isolate the problem. Attestation performance will take a small hit, but everything is ok. quick question on your analysis, do you factor in peer counts? I'm averaging 20 clients of each type, and it's about the difference between input and output of the client. It should be symmetric, but it's not so at all times, hence me debugging this. ok cool, thanks for the answer In particular: Teku is receiving more data every epoch boundary, and Prysm + Nimbus are sending more data every epoch boundary Just to tack onto the recent Chain history vs no chain history etc, I'm trying to solve this with <#688086042959806497> if you want to help be part of the solution I'd be glad to have some more collaborators. It'd be nice for all ethereum clients to be able to be able to drop 250+gb of chain history without negatively effecting the network. yeah, i wonder why there are differences
